newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent dips on profit taking after recent $2 gain.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent dips on profit taking after recent $2 gain.

text.p: IPE Brent futures slipped lower on Tuesday in a reaction to gains of nearly $2 a barrel over the past five trading sessions, brokers said.
On Monday prices jumped nearly 80 cents a barrel but on Tuesday June Brent was down nine cents at $19.63 at 1033 GMT.
Technical analysts said the market was likely to stay pinned in the $19.50 to $20 a barrel range.

"$20 is obviously a significant psychological number for Brent and after yesterday's move and ahead of the API stats it is reasonable to expect some mild consolidation/profit taking" said brokers GNI in a report on Tuesday.
In Nigeria five oil flow stations, with a production of 120,000 barrels per day (bpd), have been shut because of tribal fighting.
But no force majeure has been declared and exports are continuing normally, said Shell.
Oil dealers said they still expect thin loading programmes at North Sea fields in June with around 24 cargoes less than full output.
Also underpinning the market was a sharp rise in U.S. gasoline prices on Monday that some dealers believe could suck up to 300,000 tonnes of material from Europe during May.
But the bottom of the barrel, heavy fuel oil, remained sluggish and could keep refinery margins under pressure.
A blockade by fishing boats of the Sullom Voe Brent crude oil port continued but the fishermen said they would leave when presented with legal documents supporting an order to move.
In Texas, a fire at CITGO's 150,000 barrel per day Corpus Christi refinery was still burning after an explosion on Monday, according to local police.
IPE gas oil was down 50 cents at $173.25 a tonne for June. Dealers said premiums for physical Rotterdam barges were steady at about $1 a tonne above the screen.
Technical support and resistance for June gas oil was seen at $172.25 to $175.25 by brokers MeesPierson Derivatives in London.
